answer: In this PoA design, bonded escrows bind each identity to slashable capital, while evidence of coordinated equivocation triggers pairwise penalties: for k colluding identities, exposure grows as O(k²), not merely with each signer independently. Asymmetric depreciation then compounds losses across the swarm, creating an exponential multiplier in capital lost upon detection. This is no fable: splitting stake across sybils raises correlated risk, pushing expected returns toward nadir; umber marks the warning, not a protocol parameter.
